notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Long wide fjords with jagged green mountains rising straight from the sea; greener and more imposing than Iceland's coast.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Newer coverage comes from a blurred black pickup truck with an antenna at the front; Iceland's truck has no such antenna.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Older car coverage is a black car with a plain grey roof rack, unlike any similar-looking country.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Wooden houses, often on a stone ground floor painted a different colour, with metal or turf roofs.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Close to Icelandic, with Á, Ð, Í, Ó, Ú, Ý, Æ and Ø. It uses Ø where Icelandic uses É and Þ.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Small wooden stick bollards painted mostly yellow, sometimes with a red top.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails have yellow reflectors, which no other northern European country uses.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are yellow with a thin black border and a metal frame, much like Iceland's.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The capital is the only place with buildings over three floors, in a relatively open landscape especially to the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The second town sits on a narrow north-south fjord with fairly steep hills.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A village at the southern tip of the main island has black houses with grass roofs and a small church ruin.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Three wind parks are visible: the largest northwest of the capital, others northeast of it and east of Vestmanna.
